basis: Static source review, Rizin control-flow analysis, and an independent bounded raw-Snappy decoder. Samples were not executed and sample network endpoints were not contacted.

samples.identification: C# Microsoft Graph and ServiceNow directory audit/export utility
evidence: Main constructs HttpClient, uses the supplied GRAPH_TOKEN as a Bearer credential, substitutes supplied USER_ID into a fixed route list, and prints Graph GET responses to stdout.
The route list surveys tenant relationships, roles, owned service principals, organization, domains, sites, license details and user identifiers/counts. It does not change permissions or credentials.
A second client uses the supplied SN_SESSION cookie and SN_INSTANCE URL to GET the ServiceNow user-table CSV export; File.WriteAllBytesAsync saves it as a local CSV.

The complete source contains no token acquisition, hidden execution, persistence, destructive operation, obfuscation, or outgoing transfer of the acquired directory data. The caller supplies access and the export destination is local.
samples.change: Keep directory survey references as notable, describe their static evidence, recognize HTTP GET methods beside short-name HttpClient construction, and distinguish real C# calls from comments and strings.
samples.marker: Graph/ServiceNow audit: notable survey and accurate HTTP GET traits

evidence: The entry's CRT path reaches the concealed loader at 0x401170. It processes a vector repeatedly, decodes its native buffer, restores saved stack/register state at 0x40130d and jumps through EAX to the reconstructed buffer at 0x4ac660.

Outer VA 0x42b3d0 / file offset 0x2a7d0 begins with a 179432-byte output-length dword followed by a raw Snappy stream. Independent decoding consumes 126032 compressed bytes and recovers exactly 179432 bytes, with a PE at buffer offset 0x2e8.
Recovered PE 0x410f11 loads Mozilla NSS/SQLite and populates function slots. PK11SDR_Decrypt is stored at +0x14 and NSSBase64_DecodeBuffer at +0x18.
0x4114d2 opens signons.sqlite, supplies a SELECT for encryptedusername and encryptedpassword from moz_logins to sqlite3_exec, and supplies callback 0x411258.

Callback 0x411258 passes row fields +0x10 and +0x14 to 0x41119f, which calls the +0x18 Base64 decoder and +0x14 NSS decryptor and converts the plaintext to Unicode. The callback serializes host, username and password into Mozilla records.
0x401923 indexes AdjustKernelTableFromSSDTSpace2 during RC4 key scheduling. Its name is not evidence of an SSDT hook.

Google/Chrome resource claims conceal a native credential extractor rather than a browser. Builder and cipher-key observations corroborate CosmicDuke identity; the concrete login extraction supports the malicious verdict.
samples.change: Retire a misplaced UPX/dropper context rule. UPX names remain structural metadata; its sole download/execute consumer now requires a real UPX entry decompressor stub and writable entry. Preserve all four concrete hostile stealer/family findings.
samples.marker: CosmicDuke stealer: retire misleading UPX dropper-context trait

samples.identification: StormAttack Active Setup/service-DLL installer with erased resources
evidence: CRT entry 0x402674 calls 0x401cb0 at 0x4027a3. Configuration dword 0x404120 is 3, selecting 0x401900 then the self-delete helper 0x401390.

0x401900 creates an Active Setup Installed Components subkey, writes StubPath via RegSetValueExA at 0x401a4b, reads its own image through CRT I/O, modifies the buffer and writes a copy through fwrite at 0x401b26. CreateProcessA at 0x401b7e launches the copied path.
0x401390 obtains the current module's short path, reads COMSPEC, builds /c del with that path and invokes CreateProcessA. This is self-removal after persistence installation.

Alternate installation path 0x401260 deletes/replaces LanmanServer Parameters ServiceDLL. 0x401150 creates a host process, writes a DLL path through VirtualAllocEx/WriteProcessMemory, resolves LoadLibraryA and supplies the resolved address to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.

Resource-extraction code requests DLL resource 101. The entire 40032-byte resource section is zero, and the ten added nonstandard sections are also zero-filled. A usable embedded DLL, successful injection, and a functioning DDoS payload are not established.
StormServer.dll and the paired Storm ddos Server/welcome banners support identity. No ransom/encryption behavior is inferred from the collector filename.
samples.change: No change: existing hostile findings accurately describe retained installer/self-copy, service-DLL hijack, injection and self-delete code without claiming a working embedded payload.

rule_contracts: Directory survey matchers are unchanged; only severity and descriptions change. Bulk operations, theft and unauthorized access are not required by those matchers.

Method-specific HTTP retrieval composites move from client/managed to http/get. All exact consumers are rewritten. A bare GetStringAsync or GetByteArrayAsync method remains a neutral string/buffer retrieval observation; HTTP interpretation additionally requires HttpClient reference or construction.

C# uses structured call facts. Existing PE/DLL/PowerShell token coverage remains. Source comments and string literals no longer establish a C# retrieval call. Descriptions state co-occurrence because the current C# producer does not resolve these using-var receiver bindings.

HTTP ancestor consumers were audited. The managed HttpClient type/context observations remain in client/managed. GET selectors gain the method-specific observations; unrelated hostile claims must still supply their own required roles. A directory threshold can no longer count the moved byte token as another generic HTTP-client observation.

The removed UPX helper claimed a dropper and renamed sections but required neither. Labels and packing-token metadata remain. Its sole exact consumer retains its x86 decompressor-stub branch and intentionally loses name-only packer inference. No new UPX identity or broad exception is introduced.
Engine-emitted findings are not duplicated with YAML. No fetched dependency contributed to these three samples.

controls.purpose: HTTP constructor/call roles; cache-only near miss; comments and strings; three-resource survey versus one resource; cross-SaaS references; UPX marker versus decompressor stub versus writable entry; compiled method-token preservation. Synthetic native controls are scanned, never executed.

external_limits: The supplied Triage pages could not be retrieved. Public ML/AV scores and collector labels were not used as behavioral proof. Securelist corroborates the BotGenStudio family and Mozilla credential-stealing role; specimen behavior was independently reconstructed.
